posts.name: Dandolo
posts.cooked: Mint. A tough but fun battle Sky-Scraper fell on the last Villain turn but Guise and Cosmic avenged her. Intersestingly, at around the half-way point of the battle Cosmic was on 7 HP while Sky was at 21, but by the battle's end Cosmic had healed up to 14 and Sky was incaped. Most valuable card was Cosmic Crest; paired with a dynamic syphon on Capt. Cosmic I managed to go the whole game losing only 1 construct (and that was on the first round).

posts.name: LewdDolphin21
posts.cooked:
For once I had a mighty struggle with this one. Ultimately I got the Mint, with an incapped Captain Cosmic, 2 HP Sky-scraper, and 3 HP Guise. My first Thorathian Monolith got played right before Obvious Futility got played, so Sky-scraper took a lot of damage I hadn't intended on. Cosmic Crest didn't last, but it entered play long after Progeny had flipped and so wasn't that useful (though it would've helped with various environment things...). Ultimately I threw in a bunch of damage in the last couple rounds, thanks to the fun combination of Time of Tribulations and Compulsion Canister on Progeny.

I probably would've had a better time if I had destroyed Scion of Blight instead of Scion of Frost. This team is very good at drawing additional cards, so having to discard a card for Progeny's first turn-damage isn't as bad as it could be otherwise. It would have enabled me to do better work at hitting Progeny and keeping his HP low.

In all honesty, I'm very bad at playing Progeny. I've heard a lot of people say Progeny is the easiest difficulty 4 villain (and some say he shouldn't even be considered difficulty 4), but I still struggle with him a lot. Granted, I struggle with all difficulty 4 villains (except Matriarch, for some reason), but I've yet to figure out good strategies for Progeny.

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
Near Mint. Got him down to 4 my first try, took him out my second. Guise was a heavy damage dealer in this one, and Cosmic keeping him alive was pretty important. Repeated Thorathian Monoliths were helpful, too.

The Ziggurat wasn’t really an issue; the environment was actually pretty helpful. The real key was taking out Scion of Frost BEFORE Blight. Obviously Storm had to go second, but the first game I got rid of Blight first. If I hadn’t, I would have won; the stalling he got from his healing kept me from winning.

posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
Ugh, these decks seem intentionally engineered to limit the number of good combos available. Putting all Guise’s useless Lemme See That… cards up front was evil, and having all Sky-Scraper’s leading Tiny cards be Undetectable Relinking slowed me down a lot. The Orbital Bombardment/Obvious Futility is also suspiciously timed, almost like they wanted me to go for Monolith…

Of course, leaving Progeny with the Scion of Frost the whole game might have been a factor in my second-game loss with him at 10 HP. He ought to have flipped and done Radiant damage on himself, grumble grumble.

I did get some fun Aggression Modulator shenanigans, one medium Construct Cataclysm, and once, ONCE during that slog I had the glorious Guise the Barbarian/Blatant Reference combo, with a Dynamic Siphon to boot.

Well, next time I try, I might give everybody the Micro-Assembler to force some shuffles.

My first turn, if anyone is interested, was to put Cosmic Weapon on Guise, then on his turn he used I can Do That Too to use his base power, play the SECOND I Can Do That Too and copy Surveillance, and then use Cosmic Weapon for some decent damage.

I also had a cool turn where Guise copied Destructive Response, with Guise the Barbarian.

And I may have found a bug; if he copies Unflagging Animation, Guise hits Captain Cosmic at the end of Cosmic’s turn. It should change Cosmic’s name to Guise, so not only should it trigger at all then, it should read, “at the end of Guise’s turn, Guise deals himself 1 Infernal Damage.” He shouldn’t be hitting Captain Cosmic.
